## Problem 1.1

1.1.1 Class Definition and Constructor

```{r}
# class definition and constructor
setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(
    mean = "numeric",
    sterr = "numeric",
    level = "numeric"
  )
)

# Helper function: critical value
z_value <- function(level) {
  qnorm((1 - level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

# Helper function: check finite numeric scalar
is_scalar <- function(x) {
  is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1 && is.finite(x)
}

# Custom constructor
makeCI <- function(level, mean = NULL, sterr = NULL,
                   lb = NULL, ub = NULL) {
  
  if (!is_scalar(level) || level <= 0 || level >= 1) {
    stop("Confidence level must be between 0 and 1.")
  }
  
  if (!is.null(mean) && !is.null(sterr) &&
      is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)) {
    
    obj <- new("waldCI",
               mean = mean,
               sterr = sterr,
               level = level)
    
  } else if (!is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub) &&
             is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr)) {
    
    if (!is_scalar(lb) || !is_scalar(ub)) {
      stop("Bounds must be finite numeric scalars.")
    }
    
    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound.")
    }
    
    obj <- new("waldCI",
               mean = lb / 2 + ub / 2,
               sterr = (ub / 2 - lb / 2) / z_value(level),
               level = level)
    
  } else {
    stop("Provide either mean and sterr, or lb and ub.")
  }
  
  validObject(obj)
  return(obj)
}
```

1.1.2 Valudator

```{r}
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {
  
  if (!is_scalar(object@mean)) {
    return("Mean must be a finite numeric scalar.")
  }
  
  if (!is_scalar(object@sterr) || object@sterr < 0) {
    return("Standard error must be finite and non-negative.")
  }
  
  if (!is_scalar(object@level) ||
      object@level <= 0 || object@level >= 1) {
    return("Confidence level must be between 0 and 1.")
  }
  
  z <- z_value(object@level)
  
  lower <- object@mean - z * object@sterr
  upper <- object@mean + z * object@sterr
  
  if (!is.finite(lower) || !is.finite(upper)) {
    return("Confidence bounds must be finite.")
  }
  
  if (lower > upper) {
    return("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound.")
  }
  
  return(TRUE)
})

```

1.1.3 Show Method

```{r}
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  
  z <- z_value(object@level)
  
  lower <- object@mean - z * object@sterr
  upper <- object@mean + z * object@sterr
  
  cat("Wald Confidence Interval\n")
  cat("Confidence level:", object@level * 100, "%\n")
  cat("Mean:", object@mean, "\n")
  cat("Standard error:", object@sterr, "\n")
  cat("Interval: [", lower, ", ", upper, "]\n", sep = "")
})

```

1.1.4 Accessors

```{r}
# Define generic functions
setGeneric("lb", function(x) standardGeneric("lb"))
setGeneric("ub", function(x) standardGeneric("ub"))
setGeneric("sterr", function(x) standardGeneric("sterr"))
setGeneric("level", function(x) standardGeneric("level"))
setGeneric("mean")

# Lower bound
setMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(x) {
  x@mean - z_value(x@level) * x@sterr
})

# Upper bound
setMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(x) {
  x@mean + z_value(x@level) * x@sterr
})

# Mean
setMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  x@mean
})

# Standard error
setMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(x) {
  x@sterr
})

# Confidence level
setMethod("level", "waldCI", function(x) {
  x@level
})
```

1.1.5 Setters

```{r}
# Define replacement generics
setGeneric("lb<-", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("lb<-")
})

setGeneric("ub<-", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("ub<-")
})

setGeneric("mean<-", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("mean<-")
})

setGeneric("sterr<-", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("sterr<-")
})

setGeneric("level<-", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("level<-")
})

# Lower bound setter
setReplaceMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  
  x <- makeCI(
    level = level(x),
    lb = value,
    ub = ub(x)
  )
  
  validObject(x)
  return(x)
})

# Upper bound setter
setReplaceMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  
  x <- makeCI(
    level = level(x),
    lb = lb(x),
    ub = value
  )
  
  validObject(x)
  return(x)
})

# Mean setter
setReplaceMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  
  x@mean <- value
  validObject(x)
  return(x)
})

# Standard error setter
setReplaceMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  
  x@sterr <- value
  validObject(x)
  return(x)
})

# Confidence level setter
setReplaceMethod("level", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  
  x@level <- value
  validObject(x)
  return(x)
})
```

1.1.6 Contains Method

```{r}
setGeneric("contains", function(x, value) {
  standardGeneric("contains")
})

setMethod(
  "contains",
  signature(x = "waldCI", value = "numeric"),
  function(x, value) {
    value >= lb(x) & value <= ub(x)
  }
)
```

1.1.7 Overlap Method

```{r}
setGeneric("overlap", function(x, y) {
  standardGeneric("overlap")
})

setMethod(
  "overlap",
  signature(x = "waldCI", y = "waldCI"),
  function(x, y) {
    lb(x) <= ub(y) && lb(y) <= ub(x)
  }
)
```

1.1.8 As.numeric Method

```{r}
setGeneric("as.numeric")

setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  c(lb(x), ub(x))
})
```

1.1.9 TransformCI Method

```{r}
setGeneric("transformCI", function(x, fun) {
  standardGeneric("transformCI")
})

setMethod(
  "transformCI",
  signature(x = "waldCI", fun = "function"),
  function(x, fun) {
    
    warning("Only monotonic transformations make sense.")
    
    # Generate equally spaced points
    points <- seq(lb(x), ub(x), length.out = 1000)
    
    # Apply the transformation
    transformed <- vapply(points, fun, numeric(1))
    
    # Check for non-finite values
    if (any(!is.finite(transformed))) {
      stop("Transformation produces non-finite values.")
    }
    
    # Check approximate monotonicity
    differences <- diff(transformed)
    
    increasing <- all(differences >= 0)
    decreasing <- all(differences <= 0)
    
    if (!increasing && !decreasing) {
      stop("The function is not monotonic on the interval.")
    }
    
    # Transform the endpoints
    bounds <- c(fun(lb(x)), fun(ub(x)))
    
    # Return a new waldCI object
    makeCI(
      level = level(x),
      lb = min(bounds),
      ub = max(bounds)
    )
  }
)
```

The `waldCI` class stores the mean, standard error, and confidence level as three numeric slots. The lower and upper bounds are calculated from these quantities to avoid redundant information and maintain internal consistency. All setters validate the resulting object before returning it.

For `transformCI`, monotonicity is approximately checked using 1,000 equally spaced points within the original confidence interval. Both increasing and decreasing transformations are supported by taking the minimum and maximum of the transformed endpoints. This numerical approach does not guarantee mathematical monotonicity. For nonlinear transformations, the new mean and standard error are reconstructed from the transformed bounds.

## Problem 1.2

```{r}
# Create three confidence intervals
ci1 <- makeCI(level = 0.95, lb = 17.2, ub = 24.7)
ci2 <- makeCI(level = 0.99, mean = 13, sterr = 2.5)
ci3 <- makeCI(level = 0.75, lb = 27.43, ub = 39.22)

# Display the objects
ci1
ci2
ci3

# Convert to numeric vectors
as.numeric(ci1)
as.numeric(ci2)
as.numeric(ci3)

# Test accessors
lb(ci2)
ub(ci2)
mean(ci1)
sterr(ci3)
level(ci2)

# Test setters
lb(ci2) <- 10.5
mean(ci3) <- 34
level(ci3) <- .8

# Display the updated objects
ci2
ci3

# Test contains and overlap
contains(ci1, 17)
contains(ci3, 44)
overlap(ci1, ci2)

# Test transformations
eci1 <- transformCI(ci1, sqrt)
eci1
mean(transformCI(ci2, log))
```

All three confidence intervals are successfully constructed, and the accessors return the expected values. After applying the setters, `ci2` becomes \[10.5, 19.43957\], while `ci3` becomes \[27.43265, 40.56735\] with an 80% confidence level.

The `contains` method returns `FALSE` for both tested values, while the `overlap` method returns `TRUE`, indicating that `ci1` and the modified `ci2` overlap. The square root transformation produces a new confidence interval of \[4.147288, 4.969909\], and the logarithmic transformation of `ci2` gives a midpoint of 2.659343. Both transformations generate the expected monotonicity warnings.

These results demonstrate that all implemented methods work as intended for the given examples.

## Problem 1.3

```{r}
# 1. Negative standard error
try(makeCI(level = 0.95, mean = 20, sterr = -2))

# 2. Lower bound greater than upper bound
try(makeCI(level = 0.95, lb = 30, ub = 20))

# 3. Infinite bounds
try(makeCI(level = 0.95, lb = -Inf, ub = 20))
try(makeCI(level = 0.95, lb = 10, ub = Inf))

# 4. Invalid use of setters

# Invalid lower bound
try(lb(ci1) <- 100)

# Invalid upper bound
try(ub(ci1) <- 0)

# Invalid mean
try(mean(ci1) <- Inf)

# Invalid standard error
try(sterr(ci1) <- -5)

# Invalid confidence level
try(level(ci1) <- 1.5)

# 5. Directly test the S4 validator
try(new("waldCI", mean = 10, sterr = -2, level = 0.95))

# Check that the original object remains valid
validObject(ci1)
ci1
```

All invalid confidence intervals are successfully rejected by the constructor or validator, including negative standard errors, incorrectly ordered bounds, infinite bounds, and invalid setter operations. The direct use of `new()` also produces an error for an invalid object, confirming that validation is enforced at the class level.

Finally, `validObject(ci1)` returns `TRUE`, and the original 95% confidence interval remains unchanged at \[17.2, 24.7\]. These results demonstrate that the validation mechanisms work as intended for all tested cases.
